output.summary: In src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp, the SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter gate now accepts ANTI delim joins as well as SEMI ones. All other guards are unchanged: one DelimGet, one INNER/SEMI child join with only colref = colref conditions, and a SubqueryIsSimple RHS. Two comments were updated. With this change, a NOT EXISTS with a simple equality correlation and a filtered outer query becomes a plain RIGHT_ANTI hash join. The NDF condition is converted to =, so runtime min/max + BF filters reach the RHS scan. The q22 profile confirms that the DELIM_JOIN, the inner HJ with the delim keys and the DISTINCT are gone, and the orders scan still has min/max + BF dynamic filters. Bench: q22 150.3→106.9ms (-28.9%), then -21.5% and -23.1% on reruns. Full-run geomean -4.2%. The other templates have no NOT EXISTS and their changes are noise. q14 showed a one-off +30.3%, then +4.3% on rerun; its plan can't change.
output.generality: Helps any correlated NOT EXISTS whose correlation is plain column equality, whose RHS is simple (scans, filters, projections, inner/semi joins) and whose outer side is filtered. Anti-joins against large fact tables fall in this class. It does not apply when the correlation has extra non-equality predicates (q21 shape) or when the RHS has aggregates or other complex operators. Those keep the old delim plan. If the build side lands on the RHS (plain ANTI), no join filter is generated and the old RHS reduction is lost. SubqueryIsSimple keeps that extra cost small.
output.notes:
NULL semantics checked:
- RIGHT_ANTI keeps NULL build keys, because PrepareKeys skips null filtering when PropagatesBuildSide is true. NULL-key LHS rows are therefore still emitted by the unmatched-build scan.
- Plain ANTI gets no join filters (GenerateJoinFilters skips ANTI), and a NULL probe key with = never matches, so the row is emitted.
- The IS NOT NULL filter on the RHS replacing column makes NDF→= exact.

Checked on temp tables with NULL keys on both sides, in both build orientations (small outer and large outer), plus a correlated `<>` extra predicate. Every result matched `SET disabled_optimizers='deliminator'`.

Possible follow-up: MARK delim joins (IN / EXISTS in disjunctions) could use the same treatment, but MARK NULL semantics differ and would need their own check.
